projects.name: libft
projects.description: Custom C library reimplementing libc functions from scratch, foundation for all subsequent 42 projects.
projects.details: First real project at 42 Rio: rewrite standard library functions (string, memory, conversion, fd I/O, linked lists) in pure C without using libc. The project forced understanding what each function actually does under the hood. libft became the imported base for all following projects — FdF, CUBE-3D, and minishell load copies of it directly. Includes two parts: Part 1 (exact reimplementations like ft_strlen, ft_memcpy, ft_atoi) and Part 2 (custom utilities like ft_split, ft_itoa, ft_lstnew and the full linked list API). 41 commits over 5 months reflect continuous use as a support tool.
highlights: Reimplementation of 40+ libc functions (string, mem, lists, I/O)
Generic linked list API with ft_lstnew, ft_lstmap, ft_lstiter
Imported as base in FdF, CUBE-3D, and minishell
Zero external dependencies — no libc

projects.name: get_next_line
projects.description: Function that reads files line by line in C using static buffer and arbitrary fd, including bonus multi-fd version.
projects.details: Short 42 Rio project with surgical focus: implement get_next_line(fd) returning the next line of a file descriptor on each call, without losing data between calls or leaking memory. The core constraint is using a fixed-size static buffer (BUFFER_SIZE defined at compile time), forcing handling of residue between calls and EOF. The bonus version supports multiple simultaneous fds without interference, each with its own buffer state. Direct exercise in static memory management and block reading.
highlights: Line-by-line reading with configurable static BUFFER_SIZE buffer
No memory leaks between calls or at EOF
Bonus version: multiple simultaneous fds with isolated state per fd

projects.name: FdF
projects.description: 3D wireframe renderer in C with isometric projection, reading height maps from .fdf files via MiniLibX.
projects.details: 42 Rio graphics project: read a height map in .fdf format (grid of Z values separated by spaces), calculate isometric projection of each point to 2D plane, and draw edges between adjacent points pixel by pixel using Bresenham's algorithm. All via MiniLibX, 42's minimalist graphics library exposing only window creation, pixel writing to image, and keyboard/mouse events. Covers 3D→2D projection math, line rasterization, map parsing, and graphics event management. Includes keyboard and mouse controls for rotation and navigation. 75 commits in 2 months, with libft imported as internal submodule.
highlights: Isometric 3D projection calculated from scratch
Edge rasterization with Bresenham's algorithm
.fdf map parser with per-point height and color support
Keyboard and mouse controls for navigation

projects.name: Nebulosa Discord Bot
projects.description: Automation for tasks on a communication platform linked to a Rust game server.
projects.details: The application managed roles from a subscription system, controlled real-time finances of an in-game economy, published event announcements, and registered new players on the Rust server.
highlights: Subscription-based role management
Real-time financial control
Player registration and announcements

projects.name: Cloudflare DDNS
projects.description: DDNS client that updates Cloudflare A and AAAA records with the machine's current public IP.
projects.details: Python script that keeps Cloudflare DNS records in sync with the machine's public IP. Supports IPv4 and IPv6, authentication via API token or global API key, Discord notifications, dry-run mode, and config validation before applying changes.
highlights: Automatically updates A and AAAA records
IPv4 and IPv6 support
Discord notifications, dry-run, and config validation

projects.name: minishell
projects.description: Interactive shell in C reimplementing bash: tokenization, parsing, variable expansion, pipes, redirections, and builtins.
projects.details: One of the most complex 42 Rio projects: build a functional shell from scratch in C, capable of executing real system commands. Implementation covers the complete shell pipeline — lexer (input line tokenization), parser (command and operator tree), environment variable and $? expansion, execution with fork/execve, chained pipes via file descriptors, redirections (<, >, >>, heredoc), and signal handling (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+\). Builtins implemented from scratch: echo, cd, pwd, export, unset, env, and exit. Requires careful memory management (no leaks), process queues, and correct terminal interaction. 100+ commits in local history, published to GitHub Jan 2026.
highlights: Complete lexer + parser for tokenizing and building command tree
Chained pipes and redirections (<, >, >>, heredoc)
Expansion of $VAR, $? and handling of single and double quotes
Builtins: echo, cd, pwd, export, unset, env, exit

projects.name: CUBE-3D
projects.description: Raycasting engine in C, Wolfenstein-style: 2D .cub map rendered in 3D perspective with per-wall-direction textures.
projects.details: Advanced 42 Rio graphics project inspired by Wolfenstein 3D raycasting. From a .cub file (tile map and texture paths), the engine casts one ray per screen pixel column, calculates distance to nearest wall using DDA (Digital Differential Analysis), and determines the vertical slice height to draw. Each wall displays the correct texture based on direction (North, South, East, West). The result is a fluid 3D perspective generated entirely in software, no GPU. Includes .cub format parser for texture configuration, ceiling/floor colors, and map validation. Based on MiniLibX and imported libft.
highlights: DDA raycasting: one ray per screen pixel column
Per-wall-direction textures (N/S/E/W) mapped in software
.cub map parser with config and geometry validation
3D perspective without GPU — all calculated on CPU in pure C

projects.name: Philosophers
projects.description: Dining Philosophers simulation in C: N threads compete for N shared forks without deadlock or starvation.
projects.details: Implementation of Dijkstra's classic concurrency problem in pure C, as mandatory 42 Rio exercise. Each philosopher is a POSIX thread alternating between thinking, picking up two forks (mutexes), and eating. The core challenge is avoiding deadlock (philosophers waiting on each other indefinitely), starvation (a philosopher never gets to eat), and race conditions on shared state. Solution uses mutexes for each fork and a global state monitor for death detection by timeout. Supports configurable N philosophers via arguments, with lifetime, eat time, sleep time, and optional meal limit. Direct exercise in synchronization reasoning, memory visibility, and lock acquisition order.
highlights: Each philosopher in independent thread with think/pick forks/eat/sleep cycle
Forks protected by individual mutexes to eliminate race conditions
Death monitor by timeout without blocking philosopher threads
Configurable via args: N philosophers, times, and meal limit

projects.name: net_practice
projects.description: 42 Rio networking exercise: IP addressing, subnetting, routing, and troubleshooting across 10 progressive levels.
projects.details: Practical 42 Rio project focused on computer networking fundamentals. Consists of 10 progressive configuration levels where routing tables, subnet masks, and IP addresses must be corrected or completed for communication between hosts and routers to work. Covers CIDR, broadcast, gateway, subnetting of class A/B/C networks, and static routing. Each level is a broken network scenario that must be diagnosed and fixed, forcing reasoning about network reach and packet forwarding.
highlights: 10 levels of network topologies to diagnose and fix
Subnetting, CIDR, broadcast, and gateway in real scenarios
Static routing between hosts and routers in mixed topologies

projects.name: vps_infra_base
projects.description: Docker Compose base infra stack for VPS: Nginx TCP proxy, PostgreSQL, and RabbitMQ with provisioning scripts and CI/CD.
projects.details: Infrastructure base for deploying and testing applications on a VPS or local environment. Nginx acts as TCP proxy (not HTTP) forwarding external connections to PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ on isolated internal Docker networks, exposing mapped ports (5433 and 6380) without opening services directly. Includes Shell scripts for database/user creation and SQL migrations per project, scripts for vhost/user/queue declaration in RabbitMQ, template system for adding new projects without altering base config, and GitHub Actions deploy workflow with infrastructure smoke test. Started with simple setup and evolved with multi-project support, persistent volumes, custom Nginx error page, and network observability dashboards (Grafana, later removed to simplify scope). Collaborative: 1 external PR merged. Not production-ready without security hardening, but covers full provisioning, routing, and automated deploy cycle.
highlights: Nginx as TCP proxy for PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ on isolated Docker networks
Provisioning scripts for databases and queues per project via templates
CI/CD with GitHub Actions: deploy + infrastructure smoke test
Multi-project support without altering base stack

projects.name: SessionDB MCP
projects.description: MCP server in Python giving AI agents controlled, session-scoped access to SQL databases for real-time schema inspection and data querying.
projects.details: Exposes a SQL database to AI agents via Model Context Protocol without granting direct database access. Each connection becomes a session with token and explicit permissions (read, insert, update, delete, DDL), schema limits, timeout, and row limits. Offers tools to list and describe tables, views, functions, and relations, and to execute queries. Heavily used to provide real-time database context for a project and accelerate table creation, rules, and test verification. Not designed for production data, but could work with minimal-permission DB users and human review for destructive operations.
highlights: Session-scoped DB access with token and explicit permissions
Tools to list/describe tables, views, functions, and relations
Schema limits, timeout, and row limits per session
Multiple databases in same conversation without mixing connections
